sourceBindings.text: The trainer continues: 'Now I try the ball. If it holds, I press an even ribbon and let it break by itself. I record its length, then check the feel of a small wetter pinch. I follow both branches before writing a class. If it will not make a ball after conditioning, that is the result I record.' The demonstration must include a valid non-ribbon outcome as well as a ribbon-forming example.

units.delivery: Explain calmly and naturally to agricultural vocational learners in clear English. Read only the supplied connected passage with natural pauses. Preserve all negations, conditions, scene-safety restrictions and limits of training. Do not add medical advice, diagnoses, character voices, an introduction, music or an extra summary.

supportingCurrentSourceBinding.text: If a ball forms, place it between thumb and forefinger. Gently press with the thumb and push soil upward into a strip of reasonably even width and thickness. Let the strip extend over the forefinger until it breaks under its own weight. Do not stretch it like dough or support a long strip with the other hand and call that its unsupported length.
supportingCurrentSourceBinding.scope: Existing current-source own-weight method supports the source-equivalent snap-under-its-own-weight spoken wording; no manual pulling and no new scientific instruction.
